feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain depth and good evidence of progression. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across sections, and could sharpen impact by prioritizing outcomes over responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong career progression within NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good credibility and specificity: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, AI search, and metrics like “10,000+ page website” and “3.5 million annual page views” add substance.  
- Writing quality is polished and consistent overall, with a confident tone aligned to senior public-sector digital roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to create a tighter structure and save space.  
- Increase measurable outcomes: several bullets describe duties rather than results; add impact metrics for newsletters, campaigns, video growth, efficiency gains, or governance improvements.  
- Minor style/consistency fixes: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; punctuation/hyphenation varies slightly (“organization-wide,” “member-facing,” “front-end” are good—keep this style consistent). “Ranked among the top public universities…” in Education feels unnecessary and can be removed.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and public-sector focus. It reads well, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, so tightening it will improve distinctiveness and impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Make the opening more specific by anchoring to enterprise-scale outcomes, not just responsibilities.
- Reduce list-like phrasing; group related capabilities into a sharper value proposition.
- Use parallel structure and hyphenation consistently: “high-volume,” “public-sector,” “AI-enabled.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems for high-volume, mission-driven public-sector organizations. Combines digital governance, analytics infrastructure, editorial operations, and multimedia production to improve publishing efficiency, audience insight, and user experience, including AI-enabled search and content discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” substantially repeats Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production” is echoed throughout recent NACo roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the target roles, but this section currently overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive capability areas rather than repeating phrasing used elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, sharper labels and remove filler words like “operations” where possible.
- Prioritize the most marketable and recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and multimedia.
- Consider a cleaner version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, dashboards and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestreaming
- Standardize style: either use “and” throughout or “&” throughout; “livestreaming” is cleaner than “livestream operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization” and “AI-enabled…content experiences” closely repeat the header.
- Several items duplicate Topline Skills, especially analytics, automation, advocacy, and multimedia.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing, standardizing style, and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Standardize verbs and structure: e.g., “Built…,” “Developed…,” “Launched…,” and use consistent serial commas.
- Replace vague phrasing with sharper specifics where possible: “policy content” → “legislative and policy content”; “continued campaign growth” → “future campaign expansion.”
- Consider this tighter wording: “AI Hybrid Search: Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level chat to improve discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current NACo consultant and prior NACo role bullets.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; prioritize similarly unique projects here to avoid repetition.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and 3–4 distinct contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact and scope: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancement, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for member-facing communications.”
- Collapse overlapping duties into sharper bullets, e.g.:
- “Redesigned digital workflows, analytics, and governance models to improve cross-channel coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content architecture, and user discovery experience.”
- Replace generic phrases like “deliver technical troubleshooting” with stronger verbs and outcomes: optimize, modernize, streamline, launch, improve.
- Add metrics if possible: number of sites/pages supported, publishing time reduced, engagement gains, search success improvements, or campaign performance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Campaign/st storytelling experiences” and “AI-enabled search” duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance/analytics/workflows also overlap with Director of Digital Media; emphasize advisory/consulting scope now.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and multi-channel communications.”
- Prioritize the website transformation as the lead bullet: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page site to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-focused; add metrics if available (email growth, engagement, social reach, production volume) rather than “reaching tens of thousands.”
- Tighten remaining bullets with action + result phrasing: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio…” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership visibility and planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Governance/editorial workflow language also appears elsewhere; emphasize what changed at organizational scale here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing operational leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth at this stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social, and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets and lead with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and standardized publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership to avoid blending into adjacent NACo roles.
- Video/livestream language overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and the studio build in 2022–2024; keep this entry focused on establishing the recurring series, not broader production.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tightened to emphasize senior-level leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive language:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content strategy” to sound more senior and align with director/consultant-level work.
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Digital strategy for high-volume public-sector communications” to reinforce scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple recent work bullets; keep this item broad and avoid repeating channel lists.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to web modernization and execution leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal and CMS modernization first; they are most supported by recent experience. Consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless central to target roles.
- Replace vague “technical execution” with more outcome-oriented language such as “enterprise web delivery” or “platform implementation.”
- If space allows, add one scale cue from recent work elsewhere in the CV, e.g. Drupal modernization for a 10,000+ page site.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and more strategic.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating exact phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT,” so this section should emphasize decision-making, optimization, and business impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led wording, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Tighten to: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership dashboards • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards” or “Executive reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If accurate, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere in the CV, such as “analytics infrastructure for 10,000+ page site / 3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating every tool here if they already appear in the Technical section; prioritize strategic capabilities in Topline Skills.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older work history. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level, recent capabilities tied to the in-house studio and event production leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task-level to capability-level: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Consider adding leadership/ownership language: “In-house studio buildout and operations” if you want this section to reflect seniority.
- Drop “editing” unless paired with strategy/production ownership; it reads more junior than the rest of the CV.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Broadcast-quality video production for advocacy programming and recurring executive/event content”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with recent NACo bullets, so keep this skills item concise rather than descriptive.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior, recent digital leader, this item should emphasize strongest/current platforms and reduce lower-signal tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance and recency: “Drupal (enterprise CMS modernization) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show level/scope, e.g. “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; custom microsites)” and “SharePoint/Power Pages (internal and public-facing workflows)”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a notable project; it feels less strategic than the rest.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use “CMS Platforms” or “Web Platforms & CMS” consistently across sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same tools.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent NACo roles and projects, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as applied capabilities, e.g.: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless needed; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner and more senior.
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g. GTM used for analytics/event tracking, Workers for performance or routing, GitHub Actions for deployment automation.
- Order by current relevance/impact: JavaScript, API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, GTM, HTML/CSS, jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- GTM may fit better under analytics/measurement if that section needs strengthening.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation leadership. Since automation is already emphasized elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just names: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project operations: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most automation-relevant tools first; move Slack/Teams later since they are collaboration tools, not workflow systems.
- If true, add scope in a parenthetical for impact: “used to support editorial planning, cross-team intake, approvals, and reporting workflows.”
- Consider dropping one or two lower-value/general tools if space is tight, especially Basecamp or Trello, to keep the list more senior and focused.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Trello overlap as project-management tools; listing all three may feel redundant unless each was materially used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but the item is too generic and misses the level of ownership implied elsewhere in the CV. Since recent roles emphasize email operations at scale, this line should signal platform administration and campaign execution rather than read like a simple software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Email & Engagement Platforms:** Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope/usage context: **Platform administration, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, campaign deployment**
- Consider ordering by strongest/recent relevance: put the platform most used at NACo first
- Use consistent naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys** is cleaner and more current than “Customer Insights / Journeys”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and multiple work bullets on email/newsletters; avoid adding broad claims here that repeat those sections
- If you add campaign/segmentation language here, keep it brief so it doesn’t duplicate analytics or workflow systems items

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” It should either be tightened to emphasize optimization/measurement or reduced to avoid repeating the same platforms already proven in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Measurement & Optimization**
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • KPI design • SEO/performance analysis • A/B testing**
- Replace vague **Dashboarding** with outcome-oriented capability like **KPI design** or **leadership reporting**
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced tools first: GA4, Clarity, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio, then optimization skills

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping detail in one place and shortening the other
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already substantiated in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid listing too many generic analytics labels elsewhere

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and workflow improvements.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping launch NACo’s first in-house digital team.”
- Split into concrete contributions: “Supported web, email, social and multimedia operations; improved publishing workflows and cross-channel coordination.”
- Make outputs more specific: “Contributed to a major website refresh; produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video update for member communications.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.” Add metrics if available (video frequency, event count, audience size).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching/building the format, and the later role as scaling it.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo entries; keep this version tactical rather than strategic.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generic and underplays the podcast launch. Since later roles already cover broad digital production, this item should emphasize distinctive “firsts,” ownership, and policy/program support.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research, program coordination, and digital storytelling; launched NACo’s first podcast and led planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with clearer ownership: “Produced multimedia and digital content supporting organizational programs and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or outcomes: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or types of research/projects coordinated.
- Keep it to 1–2 lines; this is an older role, so concise impact is better than broad responsibility lists.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on podcast launch and innovation/policy project coordination.
- Avoid repeating “oversaw planning, scripting, and production” if similar production language appears elsewhere; “launched NACo’s first podcast” already signals ownership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads like a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with stronger, more recent evidence in Work Experience and Topline Skills, so it should stay concise and tool-focused.

Suggested edit
- Rename or tighten to emphasize tools, not broad functions: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Podcast editing/production”
- Replace “Livestream studio workflows” with specific tools or hardware only if named elsewhere; otherwise move that concept to “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery,” where it already fits better.
- If these tools are current strengths, consider ordering by relevance to recent work: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Livestream production • Photoshop • Illustrator • Podcast production”
